subject: Default log capture: decomposition & purge flow question
messages:
From: Elena Morales <elena@northshore.ai>
To: rafael_mendes@redwood.com
Cc: Northshore Legal <legal@northshore.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Jul 2029 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify what default logs include (requests, tokens, streaming fragments, attachments)

Hi Rafael,

We are working through our security and procurement checklist and need a plain-language summary of what Redwood stores by default for hosted API customers. Specifically:

- Do you retain the full request payload and the model-generated output (final completion) by default?
- Are streaming fragments (intermediate tokens emitted during streaming responses) retained anywhere or are they ephemeral?
- Is anything persisted from the KV cache (session-level caches) after a session ends?
- How are attachments handled if a user uploads a file as part of a request (e.g., OCR or document parsing)?
- What is the default retention period and what evidence can you provide that deletion actually occurred?

We'd like concise answers we can include in our vendor assessment; an example deletion certificate or runbook would be ideal. Also confirm whether EU data residency options are available and whether retention differs by region or deployment model.

Thanks,
Elena Morales
Information Security Manager
Northshore AI
From: rafael_mendes@redwood.com
To: Elena Morales <elena@northshore.ai>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 15 Jul 2029 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify what default logs include (requests, tokens, streaming fragments, attachments)

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front, followed by a brief explanation and next steps.

Short answers (hosted API / default):
- Request payloads: retained by default for 30 days.
- Final model outputs (completions): retained by default for 30 days.
- Streaming fragments (intermediate tokens): not persisted long-term — streaming buffers are ephemeral and retained for up to 24 hours only for troubleshooting; they are not indexed or used for training.
- KV cache: session-level KV cache is ephemeral and flushed at session end; not persisted as a customer-visible artifact by default.
- Attachments: stored as encrypted objects for the same retention window (30 days) unless you opt out; we store metadata (filename, mime-type) and a blob reference.

Explanations & mechanics:
- Retention window: the default hosted retention window is 30 days for stored request/response artifacts. This enables short-term debugging and quality monitoring.
- Deletion / proof: when a record is deleted we run a background expunge job that removes object blobs and writes a signed audit record. For customers who request deletion evidence we can provide a signed deletion certificate listing object IDs and timestamps. Typical turnaround for a hosted-account deletion certificate is 5–7 business days.
- Opt-out flags: for API customers we support a per-request header/flag (e.g., x-rw-store: false) to avoid persisting request/response artifacts. Note: opting out disables many observability features (per-route cost/latency dashboards) for those requests.
- Regional residency: you can pin your account to EU regions; data stored in an EU region will remain in EU datastores. Retention defaults remain the same unless you have a Dedicated/Private contract (see below).

Differences by deployment model:
- Hosted (standard): default 30-day retention, deletion certificate within 5–7 business days as described.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): default retention configurable by contract; typical defaults in enterprise deals are 90 days but can be reduced to customer preference and controlled by the customer's Ops team.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): retention is fully customer-managed; Redwood provides the deletion runbook and automation scripts for customer execution and verification.

Next steps
- I can loop in Kim (security) with SOC2/technical evidence and share the short retention matrix (attached). Can we schedule a 30-min call to walk legal/security through the deletion certificate example and the opt-out flows?

Regards,
Rafael Mendes
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
Attachment: retention-matrix-northshore.csv (spreadsheet showing per-deployment defaults)
From: Elena Morales <elena@northshore.ai>
To: rafael_mendes@redwood.com
Cc: Northshore Legal <legal@northshore.ai>
Date: Tue, 16 Jul 2029 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify what default logs include (requests, tokens, streaming fragments, attachments)

Thanks, Rafael — that's helpful. A couple of follow-ups from legal/security:

- Can you confirm that tokens (token-level traces) are not stored beyond the final completion record? Our reviewers are specifically worried about intermediate token exposure.
- If we choose to use the opt-out header for certain endpoints, can we still retain audit-level metadata (timestamps, request IDs) to reconcile billing and SLAs?
- For EU residency: will deletion certificates reference EU object IDs and storage locations explicitly?
- For our procurement timeline we need an SLA statement that you can produce deletion evidence within 7 business days for hosted accounts. Can Redwood commit to that in writing for our purchase order?

If you can get Kim to confirm token handling and the deletion certificate SLA language we can move this to legal review.

Best,
Elena
From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: Elena Morales <elena@northshore.ai>, rafael_mendes@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 17 Jul 2029 14:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify what default logs include (requests, tokens, streaming fragments, attachments)

Hi Elena — Kim from Security here, looping in Marissa (Compliance) as well. Quick technical confirmations and suggested SLA wording below.

- Token-level traces: We do not persist granular token-by-token traces as a separate, queryable artifact beyond any streaming troubleshooting buffer. What is stored in the platform is the original request payload and the final completion text (the assembled output). Intermediate streaming buffers are transient (kept up to 24 hours for incident debugging) and are not used for analytics or model training.
- Opt-out + audit: The opt-out header prevents storage of request/response bodies, but standard audit metadata (request ID, timestamps, status codes, region) are retained to support billing and support workflows. Those audit entries do not contain the request or completion text.
- EU deletion certificates: Yes — when your account is pinned to an EU region the deletion certificate will reference EU object IDs and the datastore location (EU region/cluster). We can provide the certificate with the storage shard IDs and a signed timestamp.
- Suggested SLA clause (hosted): "Redwood will provide deletion evidence (signed certificate listing object IDs and timestamps) for customer-initiated data deletions within seven (7) business days of the request, for data retained under the default hosted retention policy." We are happy to include this in the purchase order appendix or a SOC-addendum.

I'll attach the SOC2 summary and a redacted deletion-certificate example (SOC/evidence materials). Rafael — happy to join the 30-min call to walk through the docs with their InfoSec/legal team.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Director, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
